finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches a caller-supplied URL. The only check is a scheme prefix (startsWith('https://')), which is not a host allowlist. An attacker can point the request at internal HTTPS hosts and ports. They can also use an attacker-controlled HTTPS server that 302-redirects to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/, because axios follows redirects by default and the redirect target is not re-validated. Only the response byte length is returned, so this is semi-blind and I rate it MEDIUM. It still allows internal probing, port scanning, and size-based inference of internal responses. No authentication is visible in the code.

trace.note: const url = req.body.avatarUrl; attacker-controlled JSON body field
Only check: typeof string and url.startsWith('https://'). This is a prefix and scheme check with no hostname parsing, no allowlist and no IP/RFC-1918 blocking.
axios.get(url) runs with default redirect following (maxRedirects 5) and no re-validation of redirect hops.
Response is reduced to img.data.length, which leaks a size oracle but not the body.

finding.guards_checked: The https:// prefix check at server.js:11 does not close the finding, because the skill requires strict hostname set membership and a scheme-only check is explicitly insufficient. I found no hostname allowlist, no IP resolution or CIDR blocking, and no maxRedirects:0 setting. There is no auth middleware in the file. The route is public ingress via app.listen(3000) on the framework default binding. I did not apply Shodan reachability, since this is a code-only audit.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a scheme-prefix check, url.startsWith("https://"), at server.js:11)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from the request, server.js:11 only checks the "https://" prefix, and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get with default redirect following, so internal HTTPS hosts and redirect hops to internal HTTP are reachable, and server.js:15 returns the byte length as a size oracle; no auth middleware or host allowlist exists.
